tips.title: Rinse Before Recycling
tips.description: Always rinse food containers before recycling. Contaminated recyclables can spoil entire batches and may end up in landfills instead.

tips.title: Know Your Plastics
tips.description: Not all plastics are recyclable. Check the number inside the recycling symbol. Types 1 and 2 are most commonly accepted.

tips.title: Flatten Cardboard
tips.description: Breaking down cardboard boxes saves space in recycling bins and trucks, making the recycling process more efficient.

tips.title: Keep Paper Dry
tips.description: Wet paper cannot be recycled. Store paper recyclables in a dry place to ensure they can be properly processed.

tips.title: Remove Caps and Lids
tips.description: Bottle caps and lids are often made from different materials. Remove them and recycle separately when possible.

tips.title: Compost Food Waste
tips.description: Food scraps make up about 30% of household waste. Composting reduces landfill waste and creates nutrient-rich soil.

tips.title: E-Waste Matters
tips.description: Electronics contain valuable materials and harmful substances. Always take e-waste to designated collection points.

tips.title: Reduce First
tips.description: The best waste is no waste. Before recycling, consider if you can reduce consumption or reuse items.

tips.title: Glass is Forever
tips.description: Glass can be recycled endlessly without loss of quality. A single glass bottle saves enough energy to power a computer for 25 minutes.

tips.title: Check Local Guidelines
tips.description: Recycling rules vary by location. Check your local recycling program to know what they accept.

tips.title: Avoid Plastic Bags in Recycling
tips.description: Plastic bags can get tangled in recycling machines. Reuse them when possible or bring them to special plastic bag collection points.

tips.title: Do Not Recycle Greasy Pizza Boxes
tips.description: Food grease can contaminate cardboard. Tear off the clean parts for recycling and dispose of greasy sections separately.

tips.title: Use a Reusable Water Bottle
tips.description: Carrying a reusable bottle helps reduce single-use plastic waste and supports a more sustainable daily routine.

tips.title: Separate Batteries Safely
tips.description: Batteries should not be placed in normal recycling bins. Take them to battery collection points to prevent leaks and fire risks.

tips.title: Reuse Glass Jars
tips.description: Glass jars can be reused for storage, food containers, or small home organization before being recycled.

tips.title: Sort Waste at Home
tips.description: Set up separate bins for paper, plastic, metal, glass, and general waste to make recycling easier and more consistent.

tips.title: Check for Food Residue
tips.description: Before recycling containers, make sure they are mostly empty and free from leftover food or liquids.

tips.title: Donate Usable Items
tips.description: Clothes, books, toys, and small household items that are still usable can be donated instead of thrown away.

tips.title: Recycle Metal Cans
tips.description: Aluminium and steel cans are commonly recyclable. Rinse them first and place them in the correct recycling bin.

tips.title: Avoid Mixing Hazardous Waste
tips.description: Paint, chemicals, pesticides, and medical waste should not be mixed with regular household waste or recycling.

tips.title: Bring Your Own Shopping Bag
tips.description: Using reusable shopping bags reduces the need for single-use plastic bags and helps cut down plastic pollution.

tips.title: Recycle Old Phones Properly
tips.description: Old phones contain valuable metals and electronic parts. Send them to certified e-waste recycling points instead of throwing them away.

tips.title: Keep Recycling Bins Clean
tips.description: A clean recycling bin helps prevent bad smells, pests, and contamination of recyclable materials.

tips.title: Avoid Wishcycling
tips.description: Do not place items in the recycling bin just because you hope they are recyclable. Check the rules first to avoid contamination.

tips.title: Reuse Old Clothes
tips.description: Old clothes can be reused as cleaning cloths, donated, repaired, or sent to textile recycling programs.

tips.title: Compost Fruit Peels
tips.description: Fruit and vegetable peels can be composted to reduce food waste and create useful nutrients for plants.

tips.title: Avoid Disposable Cutlery
tips.description: Carry reusable cutlery or request no disposable utensils when ordering food to reduce plastic waste.

tips.title: Recycle Clean Paper Only
tips.description: Paper with food stains, oil, or heavy dirt may not be recyclable. Keep paper clean and dry before recycling.

tips.title: Crush Plastic Bottles
tips.description: Crushing plastic bottles can save space in your recycling bin, but check local guidelines because some facilities prefer bottles uncrushed.

tips.title: Use Refillable Containers
tips.description: Refillable containers for soap, shampoo, and cleaning products help reduce packaging waste over time.

tips.title: Separate Glass by Local Rules
tips.description: Some recycling programs require glass to be separated by color, while others accept mixed glass. Always check local rules.

tips.title: Do Not Recycle Broken Ceramics
tips.description: Ceramic plates, mugs, and tiles are different from glass bottles and usually cannot go into normal glass recycling bins.

tips.title: Reduce Food Waste
tips.description: Plan meals, store food properly, and use leftovers to reduce the amount of food that ends up in the trash.

tips.title: Label Your Home Bins
tips.description: Clear labels on your home bins make it easier for family members to sort waste correctly.

tips.title: Avoid Single-Use Cups
tips.description: Bring a reusable cup when buying coffee or drinks to reduce disposable cup waste.

tips.title: Recycle Printer Cartridges
tips.description: Printer ink and toner cartridges should be returned to collection programs or recycling centers instead of regular bins.

tips.title: Remove Tape from Cardboard
tips.description: Remove excess plastic tape, labels, or packing materials from cardboard boxes before recycling when possible.

tips.title: Buy Products with Less Packaging
tips.description: Choosing products with minimal or recyclable packaging helps reduce waste before it is created.

tips.title: Recycle Light Bulbs Properly
tips.description: Some light bulbs contain materials that need special handling. Take them to proper collection points instead of normal bins.

tips.title: Make Recycling a Daily Habit
tips.description: Recycling works best when it becomes part of your daily routine. Start small by sorting one or two waste types consistently.
